findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the 'umbrella consensus rule' explicitly (e.g., 'a majority of the cited projects collect coverage on exactly one matrix cell') so AC5 has a concrete pass condition.
evidence: AC5: 'At least three popular, actively maintained OSS projects are cited, and the remediation meets the umbrella consensus rule.'

The Plan body only says 'Compare current practice in at least three popular, actively maintained OSS projects and search tracker history' — it never defines 'umbrella consensus rule' or its pass threshold.
Undefined subjective term is not measurable/executable without clarification.
findings.finding: AC5 requires the remediation to 'meet the umbrella consensus rule', but neither the Plan body nor Context defines what the umbrella consensus rule is or what threshold satisfies it, leaving the executor to guess the pass condition.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 5: 'the remediation meets the umbrella consensus rule'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate docs/coverage.md §'CI collects coverage on the ubuntu cells only' as an in-scope edit (it asserts 'three ubuntu cells' / 'enforced three times over') and update it to describe the single primary Ubuntu 3.13 coverage gate.
evidence: docs/coverage.md:50-56 §'CI collects coverage on the ubuntu cells only': 'passes --cov on the three ubuntu cells' and 'fail_under is enforced three times over on ubuntu against the same selection'
After the change coverage runs on ONE Ubuntu cell (3.13), not three — the doc statement becomes false
The related ticket f3d4 (ropeable-hydrated-siskin) file_impact added exactly this docs/coverage.md section, confirming it is the canonical consumer of this fact
The plan says 'Change only the coverage condition' — scoping docs/coverage.md OUT despite it being a direct consumer of the changed fact
findings.finding: The plan's sole named edit target, .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml, exists and the coverage condition it changes is real, but docs/coverage.md — a consumer OUTSIDE the edited file that explicitly documents the current behavior — is not enumerated as an edit and would be left false.
findings.location: Plan step 4 ('Change only the coverage condition in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml') and AC 'Ubuntu Python 3.13 still collects branch coverage'
scenarios: A reader consults docs/coverage.md after the change and is told coverage is enforced three times on Ubuntu when it now runs once
The docs-index / drift gates or reviewers catch the stale doc and block the change the plan did not budget for
findings.suggested_fix: Add docs/coverage.md to the edit set and revise lines 50-56 to state coverage is collected on the single primary Ubuntu 3.13 cell (with the fail-under gate) and omitted on Ubuntu 3.11/3.12 and macOS.

findings.checklist_item: Require the coverage-condition change to place the flag string (never the empty string) in the `&&` slot and to verify the compiled per-cell outcome — e.g. dump/assert that exactly Ubuntu-3.13 receives `--cov` and 3.11/3.12/macOS receive none — citing the GitHub-Actions empty-string-falsy trap documented in ticket f3d4.
evidence: Current condition at .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:751 is `${{ !startsWith(matrix.os, 'macos') && '--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered' || '' }}` — a single-term predicate the new work must make compound (OS AND python-version)

Precedent ticket f3d4 landing comment: 'The second form is a silent no-op: GitHub Actions treats the empty string as FALSY, so "a && \"\" || b" evaluates to b on BOTH branches and coverage would still have been collected'
A compound predicate has more mis-orderings that short-circuit wrong; the failure mode is silent-green (coverage still collected or dropped everywhere) which the parity/focused tests may not catch
findings.finding: The plan's mechanism (a compound OS+version condition selecting --cov for only Ubuntu 3.13) is exposed to the documented GitHub Actions empty-string-falsy trap, where `expr && '<flags>' || ''` (or a mis-ordered variant) can silently evaluate to the wrong branch on every cell — collecting coverage on all/none rather than exactly one — without any test failing. The plan does not name this trap or require verifying the compiled per-cell truth table.
findings.location: Plan step 4 ('Change only the coverage condition ... so Ubuntu Python 3.13 remains the coverage gate') and step 5 ('defect-seeded mutation of the condition'); AC 'Ubuntu Python 3.13 still collects branch coverage'; workflow line 751
scenarios: Author writes `matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.python-version != '3.13' && '' || '--cov=...'` or similar, and --cov silently stays on all Ubuntu cells (no savings) or drops from all (floor un-enforced)
3.11/3.12 unexpectedly still trace, so the runner-seconds-saved measurement (AC) reports ~zero and the change looks inert
findings.suggested_fix: Write the condition so the truthy branch carries the flags, e.g. `${{ (matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.python-version == '3.13') && '--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered' || '' }}`, and in the mutation/verification step assert the resolved command line per cell (grep the executed pytest invocation in each cell's log) rather than relying solely on the parity substring test.

evidence: 5 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the runner-seconds computation: which GitHub step timings to sum, how paired same-host runs are differenced to isolate instrumentation cost, and how the aggregate is derived, so AC1/AC8 have a deterministic proving method.
evidence: AC1: 'reports per-cell and summed runner-time savings'; AC8: 'quantifies aggregate Ubuntu runner-seconds saved'.
Plan bullet 1: 'Attribute coverage overhead with paired same-host runs and current GitHub step timings' — names inputs but not the differencing/aggregation method.
A derived metric with no computation or aggregation protocol is a data-design ambiguity under E2 signals (1)/(2).
findings.finding: AC1 and AC8 require reporting 'per-cell and summed runner-time savings' and 'aggregate Ubuntu runner-seconds saved', but no computation or aggregation protocol is stated (which timings, how paired runs are differenced, how instrumentation cost is isolated from noise). The derived metric lacks a provenance/computation definition.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria lines 1 and 8; Plan bullets 1 and 5
